packets.title: core/sway-ipc + platform/sway: i3-ipc client, model derivation, fake server
packets.brief: Build SCOPE S-004/S-015 and ARCHITECTURE §6.1 as pure core plus a platform adapter. Core (`src/core/sway-ipc/`, no I/O): `frame.ts` (`encodeMessage(type, payload)` with the 14-byte `i3-ipc` header, `MessageType` enum incl. SUBSCRIBE=2, GET_TREE, GET_WORKSPACES, GET_OUTPUTS, SEND_TICK, `EVENT_NAMES`, bit-31 event flag), `decode.ts` (`SwayDecoder.push(Buffer): Message[]` tolerant of headers split across chunks, 1 MiB guard), `model.ts` (`Output`, `Workspace`, `Con`, `SwayModel {outputs, focusedOutput, workspaces, focusedWorkspace, urgent, fullscreenByOutput, windows, marksByCon}`), `derive.ts` (`deriveModel({tree, workspaces, outputs})` walking `nodes` + `floating_nodes`, app_id/`window` for Xwayland, marks collected per con), `quote.ts` (`quoteWorkspaceName` rejecting `" \ $ ; ,`, control chars, DEL, leading `--`, the reserved words `number next prev current back_and_forth next_on_output prev_on_output`), `coalesce.ts` (`Coalescer(40)`). Platform (`src/platform/sway/`): `ipc-client.ts` (one `node:net` connection, request queue, reply matching), `session.ts` `createSwaySession({socketPath = $SWAYSOCK})` with **two** connections (command + event), subscribe `["workspace","window","output","mode","binding","shutdown","tick"]` **before** the first query, 40 ms coalescing into one GET_TREE+GET_WORKSPACES+GET_OUTPUTS batch, `focusWorkspace(n)` = `workspace number n` then wait ≤500 ms for the matching `workspace` focus event or re-query, returning `confirmed|failed|unknown`; `focusContainer(conId)`; `tickBarrier(payload)` (SEND_TICK and wait for the echoed tick); reconnect backoff 250 ms→10 s with full resync; `reload` event → resync; `shutdown` → `onShutdown`. `output-pin.ts`: `pinOutput(session, name)` records focused output + con, `focus output <name>`, returns `restore()` that re-focuses `[con_id=N]` and marks the tick barrier so the focus guard ignores the dance. `fake-server.ts`: `startFakeSway(fixtures, {socketPath})` replaying recorded replies and emitting events on demand (for P-06 and P-31). Fixtures: copy `live-client-sway-tree.json` and `zenbook-0221-*.json` (paths in ARCHITECTURE §15.4) under `tests/gpuix-shell/fixtures/sway/` with a provenance comment. Tests: `frame.test.ts` (`encodeMessage(0,'exit')` bytes vs the man page), `decode.test.ts` (split chunks, event flag), `derive.test.ts` on both fixtures (nine workspaces, focused, marks), `quote.test.ts` (the 26 cases from wave1/08 `platform.ts`, reconstructed), `session.test.ts` against the fake server (subscribe-before-query, coalescing 4 events → 1 batch, verify-after-switch, reconnect). Write `src/security.test.ts` (bun, pure/static): (a) the registry contains no SECRET spec with a `cli.path`; no id named `unlock`; every ACTION spec has `confirm` set and `replaySafe:false` for logout/reboot/poweroff/suspend/hibernate; (b) grep `src/` for `nmcli … password`, `--password`, `psk=` on argv builders, `token` in log calls, `Subsonic` URLs in `console.`/`log(` calls → none; (c) `redact()` masks `password`, `psk`, `passkey`, `token`, `salt`, `u=`/`t=`/`s=` query params and clipboard/notification bodies at info level (table of 12 cases); (d) every `writeAtomic` call passes mode `0o600` and every runtime dir creation `0o700`; (e) the fence test still passes and `src/cli` and `src/daemons/core` import no `@gpuix/*`; (f) `platform/exec/runner` never uses `sh -c` for registry commands and strips `GPUIX_SHELL_SPAWN`, `GPUIX_SHELL_EXECUTABLE` and socket vars from children; (g) `validateAsk` refuses ACTION/SECRET ids and the forbidden OpenUI actions; (h) the Chrome native host accepts only the `kcmipingpfbohfjckomimmahknoddnke` origin argv and caps frames at 1 MiB. `tests/gpuix-shell/test_security.py` (hermetic + under the wrapper where a socket is needed): `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/gpuix-shell` is 0700 and every `*.sock` 0600 after core starts; a second uid cannot connect (skip if no second uid; say so); a `Notify` with a 9 KiB body is clamped to 8 KiB; a 20 KiB request line is rejected with `-32600` and the connection survives; the automation tree of the music view and the clipboard view contains no `token`/`salt` (reuse P-43/P-35 evidence `ui-tree` dumps if present, else run them); a `SECRET`-class method over the socket returns `-32001 refused`. Then `docs/gpuix-shell/SECURITY.md`: the trust boundaries (socket = same-uid local door; D-Bus roles; what the model can and cannot reach), the secret paths (wifi PSK, BT passkey, Navidrome credentials, model endpoint) and where each is read/handled/never written, the redaction rules, the exit-69 and never-both guarantees, findings with severity and owner packet (each also a BUILD-LOG request), and what was not reviewed. Acceptance: both test files green or each failure named with its owner; SECURITY.md lists every finding.

packets.title: Completeness critic: SCOPE P0/P1 coverage audit → GAPS.md with ranked gap-fill packets
packets.brief: Read-only audit (you edit nothing but the two files you own). For every SCOPE row S-001…S-202 decide, from the tree as integrated by P-30 plus the BUILD-LOG blocks written so far (re-read BUILD-LOG at the end of your pass, since the complete packets append while you work), one of `built` (code + a test or smoke step that exercises it; cite the file and the test name), `partial` (code without a test, or a test without the behaviour; say which half), `stub` (a P-00 stub still in place), `missing` (nothing), `out` (ruled out by SCOPE §21). Method: grep for the registry ids, testIds, verbs and file names each row implies; open the file; do not trust a BUILD-LOG claim without a file. Also audit the cross-cutting rules: every surface answers `ui-tree`; every surface root sets family/colour; every ACTION verb gated; every KEYS §7 verb resolves (`registry ls --json` if the CLI runs, else the specs files); the nine seam files still import every entry; `providers/index.ts` has all 18 providers non-stub; `items/index.ts` all 16; the three fragments validate; the HM module imports both P-20 files. Output `docs/gpuix-shell/GAPS.md`: a table per SCOPE section with the status and evidence per row, P0 totals (built/partial/stub/missing out of 69), P1 totals out of 65, then the ranked gap list: each gap as a ready-to-run packet brief (id `G-nn`, title, owner_paths copied from §5 so they stay disjoint, depends_on `["P-52"]`, 100–250 words naming the exact files, functions and the acceptance test) ordered P0 stubs → P0 partials → P1 missing by Tom-impact (morning hand checks first), capped at 14. Also `GAPS.json` with the same packets as an array of `{id, title, owner_paths, depends_on, stage:"gapfill", brief}` for the runner. Mark every row you could not verify as `unverified` rather than guessing. Acceptance: every S-row has a status line with a file path or the word `missing`; the P0 counts add up to 69; GAPS.json parses.

packets.title: Final integrate + deliver: green tree, MORNING.md final, logical commits, push, draft PR
packets.brief: Runs alone, last. 1. Re-read every BUILD-LOG block of wave 3 and INTEGRATION.md; apply the seam requests that remain (`providers/index.ts` additions such as P-44's `extensions`, `items/index.ts`, handler/spec index entries, the `--parse-only` flag if P-48 did not add it); keep every change minimal and list it in INTEGRATION.md under "P-52". 2. `$BUN x tsc --noEmit -p pkgs/gpuix-shell` clean; `$BUN test` green (quarantine only with a `GAPS` line); `$BUN build.ts` with zero top-level `@gpuix` imports; `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/gpuix-shell -p 'test_*.py'` green; `nix build .#gpuix-shell -L` and `nix flake check --offline --no-build` green if P-41 got there (else record the last error verbatim). 3. Under the wrapper, run `smoke_hello.py`, `smoke_rail.py`, `smoke_launcher.py`, `smoke_notifications.py`, `smoke_switcher.py`, `smoke_clipboard.py` once each and paste their `results.json` summaries into MORNING.md; do not fix surfaces now, only record. 4. MORNING.md final: status, the built/partial/not-built table (from GAPS.md, reconciled with step 3), the deploy and rollback procedure, the rulings list, the unverified list, the gap-fill packets P-51 ranked (with the command to run them), and the commit list. 5. Commits: `git reset --soft dadb1426` is **not** used if checkpoint commits exist — instead squash the `wip: checkpoint` commits into logical commits in this order with `git reset --soft` to the branch point then staged groups: (a) `docs(gpuix-shell): wave-1 notes and syntheses`, (b) `gpuix-shell: scaffold, core, platform adapters`, (c) `gpuix-shell: surfaces (rail, launcher, notifications, osd, switcher, controls, power, files, cheatsheet, ask, gallery)`, (d) `gpuix-shell: music lane`, (e) `gpuix-shell: nix package, HM module, binds, scripts`, (f) `gpuix-shell: tests, evidence, docs`. Never commit `node_modules`, `dist`, `result`, `bun.lock`, fonts, credentials or anything under `/run/agenix`; check with `git status --porcelain | grep -v '^??'` and `git diff --cached --stat`; `git check-ignore` the evidence PNGs (keep PNGs under 2 MB total, delete the rest and say so). Commit messages end with the attribution line from the session's system reminder. 6. `git push -u origin experimental/gpuix-shell`; `gh pr create --draft --base main --title "gpuix-shell: Sway desktop shell on GPUIX (overnight build)" --body-file docs/gpuix-shell/MORNING.md` (body ends with the PR attribution line); paste the PR URL into MORNING.md and NIGHT-LOG.md. 7. Append the closing NIGHT-LOG line with the time, the PR URL, and the three most important things Tom must know. Acceptance: the PR exists as a draft; `git status` clean except ignored paths; MORNING.md names the PR.
